name: Excalidraw
description: A hand-drawn-style whiteboard in the browser for diagrams and quick sketches, with live collaboration and no sign-up.

name: tldraw
description: A crisp infinite canvas for sketching, diagramming and marking up images, quick enough to open for a single idea.

name: Photopea
description: A full image editor that opens PSD, XCF and Sketch files in the browser, close enough to Photoshop to work all day in.

name: Coolors
description: Generate colour palettes with the spacebar, then check contrast and export them as CSS, SVG or a share link.

name: Google Fonts
description: Thousands of open-source typefaces to preview, pair and download, with the CSS to drop any of them onto a page.

name: Typescale
description: Build a modular type scale for a project and read off the matching font sizes, line heights and CSS in one place.

name: Squoosh
description: Compress and convert images in the browser with a live side-by-side preview; the file never leaves your machine.

name: TinyPNG
description: Shrink PNG and JPEG files with smart lossy compression, a handful at a time, and keep the transparency intact.

name: remove.bg
description: Erase the background from a photo automatically in a few seconds, with the option to drop in a fresh one behind it.

name: Cleanup.pictures
description: Paint over anything you want gone from a photo — a stranger, a wire, a watermark — and the space is filled in.

name: Unsplash
description: A huge library of free, high-resolution photographs, licensed for commercial use with no attribution required.

name: CodePen
description: Write HTML, CSS and JavaScript in three panes and watch the result update live — the front-end playground everyone shares.

name: StackBlitz
description: A full IDE in the tab that boots Node and npm projects in seconds, so you can try a framework without installing one.

name: RegExr
description: Build and test regular expressions against your own sample text, with every match explained token by token.

name: Carbon
description: Turn a snippet into a clean, shareable image with window chrome, padding and a theme — the standard way to post code.

name: JSON Crack
description: Turn a dense JSON file into an explorable node graph, so nested objects and arrays finally make visual sense.

name: Transform
description: Convert between JSON, TypeScript, GraphQL, YAML and a dozen other formats, turning a JSON blob into types in one paste.

name: Hoppscotch
description: A lightweight API client in the browser for sending HTTP, WebSocket and GraphQL requests and reading the response.

name: dbdiagram.io
description: Sketch a database schema in a small DSL and watch it become a clean entity-relationship diagram you can export.

name: CyberChef
description: The self-styled cyber Swiss army knife: base64, hashing, ciphers and dozens of other transforms, chained into recipes.

name: iLovePDF
description: Merge, split, compress, sign and convert PDFs in the browser — the everyday toolbox for any document job.

name: PDF24 Tools
description: A sprawling set of free PDF utilities, from OCR and page numbers to cropping and converting, all run in the browser.

name: CloudConvert
description: Convert between more than two hundred file formats — documents, images, audio, video and archives — and hand back a link.

name: Notion
description: Notes, databases and docs that nest inside each other, a flexible workspace you can shape into almost any system.

name: Trello
description: Boards, lists and cards that make a project's state visible at a glance — the kanban tool most people start with.

name: Toggl Track
description: A one-button timer that logs where the hours went, with reports that show which projects actually earn their keep.

name: LanguageTool
description: A grammar and style checker for English and thirty other languages, catching the mistakes a spell checker waves through.

name: Hemingway Editor
description: Paste in prose and it flags the long sentences and passive voice, grading the writing on how easy it is to read.

name: Desmos
description: A graphing calculator that plots equations as you type them, with sliders to watch a curve respond in real time.

name: GeoGebra
description: Interactive geometry, algebra and calculus tools that started as classroom software and stayed free for everyone.

name: Wolfram Alpha
description: Ask a factual or computational question and it works out the answer from curated data instead of guessing from the web.

name: Radio Garden
description: Spin a globe and drop into a live radio station anywhere on it — thousands of cities, playing what they play right now.

name: myNoise
description: Generative soundscapes for focus, sleep and tinnitus relief, each one adjustable in ten bands until it fits the room.

name: Loom
description: Record a screen and camera together and get a shareable link the moment you stop — no editing, no file to send.

name: time.is
description: The exact time in any city or timezone, to the second, with the offset and daylight-saving status spelled out.

name: Speedtest
description: The familiar download, upload and latency test, useful for proving to an ISP that the connection really is slow.

name: Jitsi Meet
description: Start a video call in a browser with no account and no download, and share the room link with as many people as you like.
